question: The same previously available encoder and share were freely chosen in both supervised menus, and improved on all three small-data roles. Does that frozen choice help with a realistic amount of training data?
eligibility: Require identical nonzero choices in the original and expanded audition, and a positive final audit gain versus the protected recipe. Freeze the elected member and its share from the confirmation file without naming either in the test. This checks the old-library winner; it does not count as Arctic promotion.
comparison: Reuse the three verified component predictions and exact fivefold shared-text partitions of the previous portfolio stability study. Collect exactly one missing fit per fold for the elected additional member, with the same production worker and held ordering. The original 8301 labelled training rows appear once out of fold per full shuffle. No new designated-validation, formal-test, H2 or earlier external development labels. The course corpus and reference scores were used in development; these are new, model-specific out-of-fold predictions, not an unseen benchmark.
gate: Always finish the five folds of the first prespecified shuffle. If the total is nonpositive or fewer than three of five folds improve, stop. Otherwise run the second prespecified shuffle. Before trying a four-member feedback policy in a real cold solve, require at least +0.20 percentage points on both complete assignments and at least seven of ten positive folds, with cluster bootstrap intervals reported for both. No adjustments of the member or probability share after observing any fold.
budget: Five or ten actual new local supervised fits, at most ten, 0 model API calls. Reuse existing 15 or 30 base component fits and report them separately.
